title: Inference API Contract and Runtime Standards (ADR + Guidelines)
author: Aisha Rahman
content:
Overview

This document records the architectural decision and prescriptive standards for the public inference request/response contract and the runtime operational requirements for model-serving at Redwood Inference. It combines an ADR (decision record), API contract specification, runtime SLOs, observability requirements, and a rollout/migration playbook. The guidance below applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments unless explicitly annotated.

Goals

- Establish a stable, versioned inference API contract that supports streaming, function/tool-calling, and structured outputs.
- Define runtime SLOs and performance knobs (batching, cache, quantization) that reduce unit cost without compromising SLAs.
- Standardize observability and error semantics so service owners and Console dashboards can reliably surface regressions.
- Provide a clear rollout and deprecation policy for breaking changes.

Scope

Applies to: 
- Redwood public inference endpoints: redwood-inference-gateway and per-customer endpoints routed via redwood-router.
- Serving runtime: serve-runtime (batcher, executor, kv-cache).
- SDKs and OpenAPI-derived clients.

Not in scope: internal admin-only debug APIs and low-level hardware kernel selection logic (kernel selection guidelines live in eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling).

Decision Record (ADR) — Summary

Decision: We adopt a versioned JSON-over-HTTP inference contract with explicit schema for request metadata, a streaming and non-streaming response model, a semantic compatibility policy (minor non-breaking vs. major breaking), and an enforced deprecation cadence.

Rationale: Versioned JSON enables broad compatibility for customers, SDKs, and tooling; explicit metadata fields let runtime components (batcher, router, cache) apply optimizations deterministically. A clear compatibility and deprecation model prevents accidental client breakage and enables safe rollout of performance-focused changes (e.g., default quantized variants).

Consequences: All teams releasing model-serving endpoints or SDKs must support the contract described below. Breaking changes require a documented ADR and a 90-day public deprecation window.

API Contract (stable schema v1)

Request (POST /v1/infer or /v1/models/{model_id}/infer)

- Headers
  - Authorization: Bearer <token>
  - X-Request-ID: <uuid> (required)
  - X-Client-Version: <sdk|app version> (optional)
  - X-Routing-Policy: latency|cost|region (optional hint to router)

- JSON body (application/json)
  - model_id: string (required unless route binds model at path)
  - input: string | {structured input as dictated by model} (required)
  - input_format: text | chat | json (optional, defaults to text)
  - max_tokens: integer (optional, default 256)
  - temperature: float (0.0 - 1.5, optional, default 0.2)
  - top_p: float (optional)
  - streaming: boolean (optional, default false)
  - tool_calling: {tools: [tool_id], intent: string} (optional)
  - cache_key: string (optional, runtime may normalize)
  - metadata: {user_tier: string, tenant_id: string, priority: low|normal|high} (optional)

Response (non-streaming)

- HTTP 200
- JSON body
  - request_id: string (echoed)
  - model_id: string
  - duration_ms: integer
  - tokens_generated: integer
  - output: string | array | object (schema depends on input_format)
  - provenance: [ {source: string, score: float} ] (optional, for retrieval-augmented models)
  - warnings: [string] (optional, e.g., truncated due to max_tokens)
  - debug: {engine_info: string, quantization: string} (restricted in private deployments unless customer allows)

Response (streaming)

- HTTP 200, Transfer-Encoding: chunked or SSE. Each chunk is a JSON object with either partial tokens or final envelope. Chunks must include request_id. SDKs must handle out-of-order control chunks.

Error semantics

- 4xx for client errors (400 malformed request, 401 auth, 403 quota, 404 model not found, 422 invalid parameters)
- 429 when rate-limited. Include Retry-After header.
- 5xx for runtime issues with a machine-readable error_code (e.g., ERR_EXEC_TIMEOUT, ERR_CACHE_MISS) and human-friendly message.

Versioning and Compatibility Policy

- API path includes a major version number: /v{major}/...
- Minor changes (additive fields, optional metadata) are backward compatible and do not require a new major.
- Major changes (schema changes that break existing clients) require an ADR and a deprecation cadence (90 days public notice + automated SDK migration where possible).

Deprecation Policy

- Deprecation announcement via Console, release notes, and email to workspace owners.
- A deprecation timeline of 90 days for public endpoints, 180 days for Dedicated/Private unless customer negotiates.
- During deprecation, the gateway must support both old and new contract with a feature flag to route traffic.

Runtime Performance Standards and SLOs

Service SLOs (applies to hosted Redwood and baseline for Dedicated)

| Component | SLI | SLO (monthly) | Error Budget | Measurement |
|-----------|-----|----------------|-------------|-------------|
| redwood-inference-gateway | p99 request latency (non-streaming) | <= 450 ms | 0.5% | gateway telemetry (edge timing) |
| serve-runtime (executor) | p95 token latency | <= 12 ms/token | 1.0% | runtime metrics (token_emit_latency) |
| router | routing decision latency | <= 30 ms | 0.5% | router logs/traces |
| end-to-end (hosted) | p99 end-to-end latency (non-streaming) | <= 900 ms | 1.0% | synthetic traces + production histograms |

Notes: SLOs are for default model family (up to 8k context on supported hardware). Models with larger than supported context must have explicit performance profiles in model catalog.

Performance knobs and recommended defaults

- Batching: Continuous batching enabled by default with target batch latency cap 40 ms for latency-sensitive routes. For cost-optimized routes, set batch_target_ms to 200 ms.
- KV caching: Enable prefix caching for chat sessions; TTL default 60s for KV entries unless pinned.
- Quantization: Runtime should expose quantization profile per model (fp16, int8, q4_0). Default for hosted is the model-author recommended profile; Dedicated customers may opt into more aggressive quantization.

Observability Requirements

Every deployed serving component must emit the following metrics with stable names and units:

- inference.request.count (counter) with labels: model_id, tenant_id, route, success=true/false
- inference.request.latency_ms (histogram) with same labels
- inference.tokens.generated (counter)
- inference.batch.size (histogram)
- inference.cache.hit_ratio (gauge) by cache_type (prefix, kv)
- inference.error.count (counter) with error_code label

Tracing and logs

- All requests must propagate X-Request-ID and standard W3C traceparent headers.
- Spans to include: gateway.receive, router.route, batcher.queue, executor.infer, executor.emit.
- Structured logs should include request_id, model_id, tenant_id, route, and stage.

Alerting thresholds (examples)

- alert if gateway p95 latency > 300 ms for 5m
- alert if serve-runtime token_emit_latency p95 > 25 ms for 5m
- alert if cache_hit_ratio < 0.2 for 10m on production workloads

Coding and API Implementation Standards

- Public handler libraries and SDKs must validate request schema at the client side and include deprecation warnings for soon-to-be-removed fields.
- Language SDKs should expose streaming in a language-native primitive (async iterators for JS/Python, channels/streams for Go/Java).
- Handlers in serve-runtime must be resilient: timeouts, bounded queues, backpressure propagation, and non-blocking logic for cache lookups.
- Critical paths must avoid synchronous blocking I/O. Use async I/O and bounded worker pools.

Infra Deployment and Capacity Guidance

- GPU pool sizing: baseline Dedicated GPU pool is sized for 3x peak QPS for supported model family to allow headroom during autoscale.
- Autoscaling policy: serve-runtime horizontal autoscaling based on tokens/sec with cooldown 60s and scale step 1 instance.
- Routing policy: prefer colocated region capacity; fallback to cross-region only when latency delta < 150 ms or capacity constrained.

Rollout, Canary, and Migration Playbook

1) Prepare: update model catalog entry, create feature flag for new contract behavior, update SDKs/docs.
2) Canary (internal): route 1% of internal traffic for 48h. Monitor errors, latency, trace spans, tail latency (p99.9).
3) Canary (customers opt-in): enable for 5% of public traffic or selected customers; gather feedback and metrics for 7 days.
4) Gradual ramp: 10% → 25% → 50% → 100% over at least 14 days with automated checks.
5) Deprecation: when final, publish deprecation notices and keep compatibility layer for 90 days.

Abort criteria (example):

- Error rate increase > 2x baseline for 15 minutes
- p99 latency increase > 30% for 30 minutes
- Any user-reported correctness/regression in quality monitoring tied to evaluation prompt sets

Appendix: examples

Sample non-streaming request (curl)

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/gptx-infer-8k/infer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"Summarize the chapter in two sentences.", "max_tokens": 120, "input_format":"text"}'

Sample OpenAPI fragment (illustrative)

paths:
  /v1/models/{model_id}/infer:
    post:
      parameters:
        - name: model_id
          in: path
          required: true
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: # simplified
              type: object
              properties:
                input: { type: string }
                max_tokens: { type: integer }

Migration checklist for SDK teams

- Add support for X-Request-ID and streaming chunks.
- Surface deprecation warnings when server sends Deprecation header.
- Add automated test harness that validates schema v1 against recorded traffic.
